---
title: "Errata for *Active Maintenance: A Proposal for the Long-Term Computational Reproducibility of Scientific Results*"
format:
  pdf:
    output-file: peer_orr_coppock_2021_errata.pdf
    toc: false
    number-sections: false
    geometry: margin=1in
---

The maintained replication code behind these errata is at <https://github.com/active-maintenance-aec/peer_orr_coppock_2021> and is archived at Zenodo at <https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24289043>, a DOI that always resolves to the latest version.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(here)
here::i_am("errata.qmd")

extraction <- read_csv(
  here::here("ground_truth", "published_claims.csv"),
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character())
)

# Every corrected value is computed from the pipeline's committed output, never typed.
text_counts <- read_csv(here::here("maintained", "output", "text_counts.csv"),
                        show_col_types = FALSE)
table_1 <- read_csv(here::here("maintained", "output", "table_1_computational_reproducibility.csv"),
                    show_col_types = FALSE)

count <- function(name) {
  row <- text_counts[text_counts$quantity == name, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(row) == 1)
  row$value
}

published <- function(id) {
  row <- extraction[extraction$claim_id == id, ]
  stopifnot(nrow(row) == 1)
  row$value_paper
}

# Entry 1: the frame the sample was drawn from.
frame_n <- count("n_study_list")
sampled_n <- count("n_sampled")
published_list_n <- as.numeric(published("eval_list_n"))
published_books_n <- as.numeric(published("eval_books_excluded"))
implied_frame_n <- published_list_n - published_books_n

# Entry 2: Table 1's percentage for resolvable errors in the archive-added column.
resolvable_archive <- table_1 |>
  filter(column == "Archive added code", row_label == "Resolvable errors")
stopifnot(nrow(resolvable_archive) == 1)
resolvable_n <- resolvable_archive$n
resolvable_of <- resolvable_archive$n_column
resolvable_pct_exact <- 100 * resolvable_archive$share
resolvable_pct <- sprintf("%.0f", resolvable_pct_exact)
published_resolvable_pct <- published_resolvable <- "74"
no_errors_archive <- table_1 |>
  filter(column == "Archive added code", row_label == "No errors")
no_errors_pct_exact <- 100 * no_errors_archive$share
no_errors_pct <- sprintf("%.0f", no_errors_pct_exact)
stopifnot(resolvable_pct != published_resolvable_pct)
```

```{r}
#| label: entries
#| include: false

# THE ERRATA SPINE. Every entry is defined once, here, and rendered from this tibble into
# this document and into the machine-readable errata_entries.csv written at the bottom of
# the file, which is what any other document carrying these corrections reads.
#
# [[...]] marks the span that changes. Each renderer supplies its own markup for it: bold
# here. Nothing else in a field is markup.
#
# Numbering follows PROCEDURES.md Stage 4b: the quantity entry, then the float entry.
# Entry 2 is class float because the claim it corrects is a cell of Table 1, which has no
# row in the extraction and so no block in in_text_claims.R; the ground truth compares the
# cell directly against the published transcription.
#
# claim_ids is the semicolon-separated list of ground-truth claim_id values the entry
# corrects. corrected_values runs parallel to it, one value per id, built from the same
# expression that builds the marked span of the corrected sentence.
cv_frame <- as.character(frame_n)

entries <- tribble(
  ~entry, ~class, ~source, ~form, ~title, ~location, ~published, ~corrected, ~note, ~claim_ids, ~corrected_values,

  1, "quantity", "pipeline", "full",
  "The number of studies the sample was drawn from",
  "p. 463, Evaluation",
  "We compiled a list of [[all 97]] archived studies[[, excluded three books,]] and then randomly selected 20 studies (Peer, Orr, and Coppock 2021).",
  str_glue("We compiled a list of [[{cv_frame}]] archived studies and then randomly selected 20 studies (Peer, Orr, and Coppock 2021)."),
  str_glue(
    "The sentence implies a sampling frame of {implied_frame_n} studies, {published_list_n} less ",
    "{published_books_n} books. The study list the sampling script reads, ",
    "ISPSDataArchive_StudyList_20191108.csv, has {frame_n} rows, and drawing {sampled_n} from ",
    "that list with the seed and sampler the authors used returns exactly the {sampled_n} study ids ",
    "the deposit carries. The list has no field marking a book. The published {published_list_n} ",
    "and {published_books_n} books cannot be reconciled with the {frame_n}-row list from the ",
    "deposited or archived materials, so either the total or the exclusion count is misstated, ",
    "and the corrected sentence states only what the materials show. The sample of {sampled_n}, ",
    "its selection, and every count computed from it are unaffected."),
  "eval_list_n",
  cv_frame,

  2, "float", "pipeline", "brief",
  "A percentage printed one point too high in Table 1",
  "p. 464, Table 1",
  "Resolvable errors, Archive Added Code: 8 ([[74]]%)",
  str_glue("Resolvable errors, Archive Added Code: 8 ([[{resolvable_pct}]]%)"),
  str_glue(
    "{resolvable_n} of {resolvable_of} studies is {sprintf('%.1f', resolvable_pct_exact)} per ",
    "cent, which rounds to {resolvable_pct}. The neighbouring cell, 3 (27%), is ",
    "{sprintf('%.1f', no_errors_pct_exact)} per cent and is rounded correctly, and the column's ",
    "two percentages, {no_errors_pct} and {resolvable_pct}, then sum to 100. The count of ",
    "{resolvable_n} is right."),
  "table_1_archive_resolvable_errors_pct",
  NA_character_,

  3, "bibliographic", "reference_audit", "brief",
  "The Gertler and Bullock reference prints a first page in place of a page range",
  "p. 465, References",
  "Gertler, Aaron L., and John G. Bullock. 2017. “Reference Rot: An Emerging Threat to Transparency in Political Science.” PS: Political Science & Politics 50 (1): [[166]].",
  "Gertler, Aaron L., and John G. Bullock. 2017. “Reference Rot: An Emerging Threat to Transparency in Political Science.” PS: Political Science & Politics 50 (1): [[166--71]].",
  str_c(
    "Crossref, doi 10.1017/s1049096516002353, gives the article's pages as 166 to 171. The ",
    "corrected range keeps the reference list's own style, which drops the leading digits a ",
    "last page shares with the first (Alvarez, Key, and Núñez 2018 prints 422–26)."),
  NA_character_,
  NA_character_
) |>
  mutate(across(c(title, published, corrected, note, claim_ids, corrected_values), as.character))

stopifnot(nrow(entries) == max(entries$entry), !anyDuplicated(entries$entry))

# values_in_spans is NA for an entry with no values, and TRUE where the value is the token
# the sentence prints.
entries <- entries |>
  mutate(values_in_spans = if_else(is.na(corrected_values), NA, TRUE))

# Gate: corrected_values agrees with the sentence it was glued into ----
marked_spans <- function(x) str_match_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]")[[1]][, 2]

quantified <- entries |>
  filter(!is.na(corrected_values), values_in_spans) |>
  mutate(ids = str_split(claim_ids, ";"), values = str_split(corrected_values, ";"),
         spans = map(corrected, marked_spans))

stopifnot(all(lengths(quantified$ids) == lengths(quantified$values)))

value_placed <- pmap_lgl(quantified, function(...) {
  e <- list(...)
  if (length(e$values) == length(e$spans)) {
    all(map2_lgl(e$values, e$spans, \(v, s) str_detect(s, fixed(v))))
  } else {
    all(map_lgl(e$values, \(v) any(map_lgl(e$spans, \(s) str_detect(s, fixed(v))))))
  }
})

if (!all(value_placed)) {
  print(quantified |> filter(!value_placed) |> select(entry, title, corrected_values, corrected))
  stop("An entry's corrected_values are not in the spans of its corrected sentence.")
}

has_ids <- !is.na(entries$claim_ids) & nzchar(entries$claim_ids)
stopifnot(
  all(!is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$class == "quantity" & entries$form != "note" & has_ids])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values[entries$class != "quantity" | entries$form == "note"])),
  all(is.na(entries$corrected_values) | has_ids)
)

# Every id an entry corrects must be a real claim. The extraction holds the prose claims;
# Table 1's cells live in the published transcription of the table.
table_cells <- read_csv(here::here("ground_truth", "published_maintext_tables.csv"),
                        col_types = cols(.default = col_character()))
cited_ids <- entries$claim_ids |>
  str_split(";") |>
  unlist() |>
  str_trim() |>
  discard(\(x) is.na(x) | x == "")
stopifnot(all(cited_ids %in% c(extraction$claim_id, table_cells$claim_id)))

# The published token the entry corrects must be the one the transcription records.
stopifnot(published("eval_list_n") == "97",
          table_cells$value_paper[table_cells$claim_id == "table_1_archive_resolvable_errors_pct"] ==
            published_resolvable_pct)

bold <- function(x) str_replace_all(x, "\\[\\[(.*?)\\]\\]", "**\\1**")
```

Two corrections to the *PS: Political Science & Politics* article
`r "10.1017/S1049096521000366"`. Neither changes a conclusion of the article. Every corrected value
below is computed at render time from a full reproduction of the published counts, held in the
repository `active-maintenance-aec/peer_orr_coppock_2021`. Bold marks the tokens that changed;
everything else in each corrected sentence is the published wording.

```{r}
#| label: render-entries
#| echo: false
#| results: asis

# A heading is only a heading when a blank line precedes it, so every entry opens with one.
walk(seq_len(nrow(entries)), function(i) {
  e <- entries[i, ]
  cat("\n\n## ", e$entry, ". ", e$title, "\n\n> ", bold(e$published),
      "\n\n**Corrected:** ", bold(e$corrected), "\n\n", e$note, "\n", sep = "")
})
```

```{r}
#| label: emit-spine
#| include: false

stopifnot(
  all(entries$class %in% c("quantity", "description", "interpretation", "definition", "label", "float", "cross_reference", "wording", "spelling", "typography", "bibliographic")),
  all(entries$form %in% c("full", "brief", "note")),
  all(entries$source %in% c("pipeline", "reading", "reference_audit", "publisher_record", "authors_archive", "proof"))
)
write_csv(entries, here("errata_entries.csv"))
```
